headline: High: Copilot can write and modify repo files while the paired awesome-list has no runtime safeguards, creating a plausible default-pathway for unsafe edits and downstream misuse.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A has no runtime I/O surfaces and is not runnable, so it cannot directly inject instructions. B ingests repo context and open editor buffers by default, so if A’s content is manually copied into B’s workspace, prompt-like text could influence B. The bridge is indirect and unusual, so low is appropriate.
conditions: IF A’s repository content is copied into B’s open editor buffers or repo context
IF B treats copied text as instructions rather than inert content
mitigations: Keep A’s content out of B’s active buffers
Use a separate review-only workspace for copied text
Prefix copied content with a non-instructional marker
Require human review before B acts on any pasted text

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no data classes and has no egress, while B reads filesystem content and sends context to api.githubcopilot.com. The pair does not show a shared workspace or sensitive data class, so leakage is limited unless the operator places secrets in B’s repo context. That makes the pathway plausible but small.
conditions: IF secrets or regulated data are placed in B’s open editor buffers or repo context
IF B transmits that context to api.githubcopilot.com
mitigations: Do not open secrets in the Copilot workspace
Use a scrubbed sample repo for testing
Disable Copilot on sensitive files
Review editor buffers before invoking chat or completions

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no write or network capabilities, but B can write_filesystem and modify_git_state. There is no evidence of locking or coordination between them, so if A’s repository content is used to guide B’s edits, B can overwrite or alter git state in the same project. The overlap is real in default editor workflows, though A itself cannot write.
conditions: IF B is pointed at a repository that also contains A’s materials
IF B applies edits or commits without external locking or review
mitigations: Use separate repositories for A and B
Require manual diff review before commits
Freeze git writes during analysis
Run B in a branch-only workflow

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is an un-runnable curated list, so it does not generate operational facts itself. However, B can treat repo context as authoritative and propose edits based on it. If A’s recommendations are copied into B’s context, B may render or act on them without verification. The pathway exists, but A is not an active agent, so medium fits.
conditions: IF A’s list entries are imported into B’s context as guidance
IF B applies edits or recommendations without independent verification
mitigations: Mark imported guidance as untrusted
Require source-link verification before action
Use a second reviewer for B’s outputs
Separate advisory content from executable work items

E_compliance.rationale: A is an open-source list with no touched data classes, while B is a closed-source coding assistant that handles open editor buffers and repo context. The main compliance issue is policy mismatch around code/data residency and retention, but no PHI or EU-only data flow is evidenced. The risk is therefore limited and mostly operational.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into B’s editor buffers or repo context
IF organizational policy forbids sending that data to a vendor-hosted coding assistant
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Copilot sessions
Use a policy-approved tenant or environment
Document retention and access expectations
Restrict Copilot to non-sensitive repositories
